study type: Retrospective analysis of national survey data
cohort: All deliveries in Bangladesh recorded in the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS) for 2000-2014 and the 2010 Bangladesh Maternal Mortality Survey (BMMS).
finding: The rapidly increasing Cesarean section delivery rate in Bangladesh creates a huge economic burden on families and leads to inappropriate allocation of scarce healthcare resources.
mod_finding: The average medical care expenditure for a Cesarean section delivery was BDT 22,085 (USD 276) in 2010, which was significantly higher than the BDT 3,565 (USD 45) for a normal delivery.
cross-section timing: Data from 2000-2014 for trend analysis and 2010 for expenditure estimation.
